newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat steady, barley slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: French wheat steady, barley slightly firmer.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Tuesday with exporters still in the dark over the outcome of a wheat tender launched by Iraq, dealers said.
A lack of fresh offtake was also starting to weigh on market sentiment, they said.
Meanwhile barley prices slightly firmed as exporters started to get cover on recent sales to Saudi Arabia.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 865 francs per tonne for January delivery and at 860 francs per tonne for February delivery, both unchanged on Monday.
February barley into Rouen was bid at 860 francs per tonne, a level offered on Monday for spot barley.
"The barley market is opening up," one dealer said.
In the port of Dunkirk favoured for exports to Saudi Arabia because of it can handle large cargoes, dealers said buyers were asking for prices.
In early January Saudi Arabia bought 1.2 million tonnes of feed barley for February and March. The bulk of the grain was expected to come from the European Union.
But exporters did not rush to secure export licences from the European Union to cover the sale.
But they are expected to start bidding for these licences at this week's EU grain auction.
